sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Origin**: Founded by **Dantidurga** (c. 735–756 AD) who overthrew the Chalukyas of Badami. Capital: **Manyakheta** (modern Malkhed).
• **Tripartite Struggle**: Key participants alongside Palas and Pratiharas for control over **Kannauj**, the symbol of imperial legitimacy.
• **Religious Policy**: Known for **religious eclecticism**; patronized Shaivism, Vaishnavism, and Jainism. Arab travelers (e.g., Sulaiman) praised their tolerance.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The Rashtrakutas maintained a massive standing army and a sophisticated bureaucracy, often employing feudatories (Samantas) for regional administration.

items.definition: The capital city established by Amoghavarsha I; became a center of trade and culture.
The earliest available work on poetics in Kannada, authored by Amoghavarsha I, highlighting the rise of regional languages.
Feudal lords who provided military support in exchange for land grants, a precursor to later medieval feudal structures.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Literary Patronage**: Promotion of Kannada and Sanskrit literature (Pampa, Ponna, Ranna - the 'Three Gems').
• **Diplomatic Ties**: Maintained active trade and diplomatic relations with the Abbasid Caliphate.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Constant warfare on two fronts (North vs. Palas/Pratiharas; South vs. Pallavas/Cholas) led to resource exhaustion.
• **Solutions**: The dynasty eventually collapsed due to internal rebellions and the rise of the Later Chalukyas.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'D-K-A' (Dantidurga, Krishna I, Amoghavarsha).
• **Decoded Meaning**: D (Founder), K (Kailasa Temple builder), A (Author of Kavirajamarga/Greatest King).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the Rashtrakutas with the Chalukyas. Remember: Rashtrakutas succeeded the Chalukyas of Badami, but were distinct from the Eastern Chalukyas.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Cosmopolitan Deccan' to describe the Rashtrakuta state, highlighting their synthesis of North-South cultural and political traditions.

keyTakeaways: Rashtrakutas were the primary power brokers in the Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj.
They were pioneers in rock-cut architecture, specifically the Kailasa temple at Ellora.
Their reign marked the 'Golden Age' of Kannada literature and religious pluralism.
